q: Batteries and electric generators are called sources of ____ force. 2024
e: Batteries and generators supply electrical energy by converting other energy forms, providing electromotive force.

q: An electric light bulb is made of a glass bulb consisting of a ____ filament. 2024
e: Tungsten is chosen as a light bulb filament due to its high melting point and resistance.

q: Electrical energy is energy associated with the flow of charge through any part of ____. 2024
e: Electrical energy is work done as electric charges flow through an electric circuit.

q: The potential difference is the amount of ____ required to move a unit charge from one end to another end of a circuit element. 2025
e: Potential difference equals work done or energy required per unit charge.

q: If a 1200 W electric ion is used for 50 min, the electricity meter reading increases by ____ unit. 2025
e: Energy consumed = Power × time = 1.2 kW × (50/60) h = 1 kWh = 1 unit.

q: When a current flows through the nichrome coil of an electric stove, it produces ____ energy. 2026
e: An electric stove converts electrical energy into heat energy via Joule heating.

q: The sources of electromotive force convert ____ from some other forms into electrical form. 2025
e: Sources of electromotive force transform mechanical, chemical, or solar energy into electrical energy.

q: Electrical ____ is the rate of transfer of electrical energy. 2025
e: Electrical power is defined as the rate at which electrical energy is transferred.

q: Electrical power is the rate of transfer of ____. 2025, 2026
e: Power measures how quickly electrical energy is used or transferred over time.

q: The practical unit of electrical energy is ____. 2025
e: Kilowatt hour (kWh) is the commercial practical unit used to measure electrical energy.

q: Electrical ____ is the rate of transfer of electrical energy. 2026
e: Electrical power measures energy converted per unit time.

q: James Prescott Joule in 1841 experimentally studied the ____ effect of electric current. 2026
e: Joule experimentally determined the relation between current, resistance, and heat produced.

q: The total work done in moving a unit positive charge round the complete circuit is ____. 2025
c: electromotive force of the battery (or) IR + Ir
e: Work done per unit charge across external and internal circuits equals the source electromotive force.

q: ____ is a good electrical insulator and can withstand very high temperature. 2025
e: Mica provides excellent electrical insulation while tolerating elevated temperatures.

q: Electromotive force is a ____ quantity. 2025
e: Electromotive force represents energy per unit charge, which has magnitude only.

q: The practical unit of electrical energy is ____. 2025
e: The standard practical commercial unit for electrical energy consumption is kWh.

q: The heating effect of electric current in a resistor is given by the formula ____. 2025
e: Heat generated H is proportional to current squared, resistance, and time divided by Joule's constant J.

q: The rate at which electrical energy is converted into heat in a resistor is called ____ and is measured in watts. 2025
e: Rate of energy conversion in a resistor is defined as electrical power.

q: The electric light bulb converts most of the electrical energy into ____ and light energy. 2026
e: In incandescent lamps, a large percentage of electrical energy dissipates as heat.

q: The practical unit of electrical energy is ____. 2025
e: Kilowatt hour is used by electric utility companies to bill energy usage.

q: The total electrical energy consumed in a circuit is measured in ____. 2025
e: Electrical energy consumption over time is measured in kWh.

q: Electrical power can be expressed as the product of ____ and current. 2025
e: Electrical power formula is P = V × I.

q: The electrical energy is related to the amount of heat as ____. 2025
e: Work done W equals heat produced H multiplied by Joule's mechanical equivalent J.

q: The two batteries have equal emfs and equal internal resistances, the current flowing through each battery is ____. 2025
e: When two identical batteries are in parallel, each carries half of the total current.

q: For appliances above 700 W, a ____ fuse should be fitted. 2025
e: Appliances drawing higher power require a 13 A safety fuse.

q: Batteries and ____ are called sources of electromotive force. 2025
e: Both batteries and generators maintain potential differences as sources of emf.

q: Generally, a source of electromotive force has an internal ____. 2025
e: Real voltage sources possess internal resistance that causes voltage drop under load.

q: Electrical ____ is the rate of transfer of electrical energy. 2025
e: Rate of doing work or transferring energy in a circuit is power.

q: The tungsten filament becomes hot when a ____ flows through it. 2025
e: Electric current flowing through high-resistance filament generates heat.

q: A ____ is a thin short wire of tin-lead alloy. 2025
e: A fuse contains a short wire made of low-melting tin-lead alloy to protect circuits.

q: Joule's law of electricity and heat is given by ____. 2025
e: Joule's law formula relates heat produced to current, resistance, and duration.

q: Batteries and generators are called sources of ____ force. 2025
e: Sources providing electrical potential difference are sources of electromotive force.

q: The unit of electrical power is the ____. 2025
e: The standard SI unit for electrical power is the watt (W).

q: In parallel connection of batteries, care must be taken that the terminal of the ____ polarity should be connected together. 2026
e: Parallel battery connections require joining terminals of the same polarity together.

q: Mica is a good electrical ____ and can withstand very high temperature. 2026
e: Mica acts as a heat-resistant electrical insulator in electric heating devices.

q: A 1200 W electric kettle is used for 50 minutes. The electricity consumed is ____ kWh. 2026
e: Energy = 1.2 kW × (50/60) h = 1 kWh.

q: 1 kWh of electrical energy is equal to ____ J. 2026
In the lighting circuit there are only two wires, live and ____. 2026
e: Standard lighting circuits consist of a live wire and a neutral wire.

q: In charging a battery, the potential difference between the terminals is equal to ____. 2026
e: During battery charging, terminal voltage V equals emf E plus internal resistance drop Ir.

q: Electric light bulbs are of various ____ and electrical power. 2026
e: Light bulbs are manufactured in various physical sizes and power wattage ratings.
